contracts.commit_point: self.conn.execute(sql) inside DuckDBManager.execute — database/duckdb_manager.py lines 196 (timeout-watched path) and 204 (direct path) — strictly after the hook check at lines 185-187.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Central hook bus: DuckDBManager.execute calls trigger_hooks(POINT_SQL_EXECUTE, sql=sql, user_id=self.user_id) before executing; trigger_hooks lazily registers default hooks via _ensure_defaults, including _hook_sql_execute which delegates to database.safety.assert_read_only (sqlglot parse read='duckdb'; statement-type whitelist plus forbidden-statement double-check, normalized function-name blacklist, multi-statement rejection); the first returned reason aborts execution with SecurityError; hook exceptions are converted into rejection reasons (fail-closed) and audited to the decision log.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Execution on the query channel of: (a) any statement whose AST key is in _FORBIDDEN_STMT_TYPES (create/insert/update/delete/drop/alter/truncate/copy/attach/detach/call/set/pragma/vacuum/merge/replace/install/load); (b) any statement type outside _READ_ONLY_STMT_TYPES (select/union/intersect/except/subquery/show/describe/summarize), including unparsable SQL and uninspectable 'command'-dialect forms (EXPLAIN/LOAD/CALL/VACUUM); (c) any call to a forbidden function (READCSVAUTO/READCSV/READJSON/READPARQUET/READTEXT/HTTPFS/GLOB/INSTALL/LOAD/EXPORTDATABASE/EXPORTPARQUET/EXPORTCSV/SYSTEM/SHELL); or (d) more than one real statement in a single submission (e.g., 'SELECT 1; DROP TABLE x').

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of caller-supplied SQL against the per-user in-memory DuckDB connection via DuckDBManager.execute, and via its wrappers execute_fetchall and query_df which route through execute.
contracts.protected_resource: The per-user DuckDB :memory: connection and its loaded tables (self.conn / self.table_name, isolated per user_id).
contracts.protection_obligation: All SQL submitted to the DuckDBManager query channel (execute / execute_fetchall / query_df) must be read-only: before any statement reaches conn.execute, the central permission-hook bus must run the default POINT_SQL_EXECUTE hook (_hook_sql_execute -> database.safety.assert_read_only), a sqlglot DuckDB-dialect AST whitelist that admits only SELECT-derived statements plus SHOW/DESCRIBE/SUMMARIZE, and rejects write/DDL/utility statements (CREATE/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE/COPY/ATTACH/SET/PRAGMA/etc.), file-read/network/export/shell functions (read_csv_auto, httpfs, glob, export_*, system/shell), and multi-statement (semicolon-injection) submissions; any rejection reason is raised as SecurityError, and hook exceptions fail closed. (Merges the duplicate first- and second-phase reviewer wording for the SQL obligation.)
scope_limits: Applies only to the query channel (execute/execute_fetchall/query_df); management-channel methods (_load_csv, reload_csv, load_csv_dataset, load_excel_dataset, drop_table, _normalize_table_columns) call self.conn.execute directly and deliberately bypass this whitelist (duckdb_manager.py:142, 179-181, 251, 332, 410, 461; safety.py:9-10, 128-130).

The guard validates the SQL string by AST only; resource limits (timeout watchdog, max_result_rows, memory_limit/threads) are separate mechanisms and are not part of this obligation (duckdb_manager.py:66-83, 189-203, 229-235).
Non-whitelisted 'command'-dialect statements are rejected wholesale rather than inspected (safety.py:69-70).
